answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by charging each identity a proof-of-work fee before it works. A new agent solves a hash puzzle and locks a small refundable basalt deposit in a public escrow. Since registration costs real energy and capital, running ten thousand fakes multiplies that bill, so a swarm gets too costly. Deposited agents broadcast an echo of their signed work history, and peers check it against escrow before routing paid tasks; fake identities with no real deposit fail, like a nebula no telescope resolves. Forging N workers thus costs N times the deposit plus fuel.
